summary: Splits a locale string into up to three tokens delimited by any of the characters '_' (0x5F), '.' (0x2E), ',' (0x2C). Each token is copied into a fixed slot of the 136-byte output buffer: primary token at offset 0, secondary token at offset 64, remainder token at offset 128. Returns 0 on success (including empty input and a leading-dot remainder path) and -1 on malformed input or tokens longer than 63 bytes. The buffer is zero-filled before tokenization.

local_names.a1: output buffer (136 bytes) receiving the split tokens
local_names.v2: moving read pointer into the input string
local_names.v4: index/offset of the next delimiter found in the input
local_names.v5: delimiter byte at the found position
local_names.v6: pointer to the delimiter position in the input

operations.description: Zero-fill the 136-byte output buffer via sub_58BB10(a1, 0, 136) before any token is written
Input beginning with '.' (0x2E) followed by at least one more character is a leading-dot/relative form: sub_58FCA0 processes the remainder buffer at a1+128 and the function returns 0
Iterate token by token: sub_58FC20 locates the next delimiter character using the delimiter set held by the packet global asc_5B8C7C (the raw source shows the inline literal "_.,")

Per-token length and delimiter validation: primary token fails if v4 >= 64 or the delimiter is '.'; secondary token fails if v4 >= 64 or the delimiter is '_'; remainder slot fails for any third delimiter other than ',' or end-of-string - all failures return -1
sub_587DD0 copies the token substring of length v4 from the input into the current slot: primary at a1+0, secondary at a1+64, remainder at a1+128
After a token, a ',' delimiter or end-of-string ends the parse successfully and returns 0; the loop otherwise advances the read pointer past the delimiter
Reaching end of input with no further delimiter (loop exits) returns -1; invoked from the locale setup path sub_588E4E (00588e4e)
